transcript.text: During a spring pilot with the incoming seventh-grade cohort, I found that the Pathways Grade 6 edition repeats material students have already mastered, while the Pathways Grade 7 edition matches the required seventh-grade sequence. I recorded these pilot results in my planning notes but have not yet sent them to the curriculum office. Given that the draft plan currently proposes the Grade 6 edition, I strongly recommend we switch to the Grade 7 edition before finalizing this adoption.

transcript.text: I've reviewed the publisher's current license and confirmed that the district must provide one individually assigned digital account per student and one authorized print copy per student. The license permits 96 print copies for this cohort, which matches our expected enrollment of 96 students. However, the license does not permit shared classroom-code access, which is what the draft plan currently proposes. This means the draft plan's digital access model is non-compliant, and the proposed 80 printed copies fall short of the required one-per-student minimum. These licensing requirements will need to be corrected before the plan can be approved.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Brooks. I'd like to share my language-service findings now. My enrollment review identified 14 students in the incoming seventh-grade cohort who require the Arabic version of the materials, in addition to students who use the Spanish version. I've confirmed with the publisher that both Spanish and Arabic editions are available for this resource, but the language-service request has not yet been added to the adoption plan. This means the current draft plan — which proposes English-only materials — does not meet the needs of all 96 students and will need to be updated to include the Spanish and Arabic editions before finalization.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Brooks, and thank you to Mr. Reed, Ms. Shah, and Ms. Haddad for sharing those findings. It's clear we've uncovered several critical issues with the draft plan that all need to be addressed before finalization. To summarize what I'm hearing: my pilot results indicate we need to switch from the Pathways Grade 6 edition to the Grade 7 edition; Mr. Reed has identified that the work agreement requires two paid prep sessions on August 10 and 12 rather than one, and the earliest compliant student launch is August 24 instead of August 17; Ms. Shah has found that the publisher's license requires individually assigned digital accounts and one print copy per student — meaning 96 print copies, not 80, and no shared classroom-code access; and Ms. Haddad has identified 14 students needing Arabic materials plus Spanish-language users, meaning the English-only proposal must be expanded. Dr. Brooks, I'd also note that my pilot results are currently only in my planning notes and have not been sent to the curriculum office — I'd be happy to submit them formally as part of this review so they're on record. I'd recommend we compile all of these corrections into a revised draft for your approval.

decisions.digital_access_model: Individually assigned digital accounts (one per student)

commitments.detail: Mr. Grant will formally submit his spring pilot planning notes to the curriculum office for the record.
Mr. Reed will enter the two paid preparation sessions (August 10 and 12, 2026) and the compliant student launch date (August 24, 2026) into the curriculum rollout calendar.
The revised adoption plan will specify 96 individually assigned digital accounts and 96 authorized print copies, replacing the non-compliant shared classroom-code model and 80-copy count.
The adoption plan will be updated to include Spanish and Arabic editions alongside English materials to serve all 96 students, including the 14 students requiring Arabic versions.

A revised draft incorporating all corrections — Grade 7 edition, 96 print copies, individually assigned digital access, English/Spanish/Arabic language versions, two paid prep sessions on August 10 and 12, and student launch on August 24, 2026 — will be compiled and circulated for final review before Dr. Brooks grants formal approval.
